title: Reject a bad request without losing the last accepted graph
prompt: loadRequest reads whitespace-separated unsigned fields: vertices edges source target, then exactly edges triples from to weight. Bounds: 1..128 vertices, <=4096 edges, endpoints <vertices, weights <=1000000. Digits only: reject signs, suffixes, missing/trailing fields with invalid_argument. Commit only after the entire request validates. Duplicate directed edges are allowed.
signature: struct Request; void loadRequest(std::string_view text,Request& accepted)

tests.label: Signed field
tests.hint: Digits only, not a signed parser.

tests.label: Duplicate edges allowed
tests.hint: Do not drop an input edge.

tests.label: Weight limit
tests.hint: Check before accumulating beyond the bound.

hints: A candidate object protects the old accepted state on parsing failure.
The digit>limit check must happen before limit-digit, because size_t is unsigned.
explanation: Parsing, validation, and commit are separate phases. A bounded digit loop rejects a numeric prefix such as 5x and prevents overflow. The final move is nonthrowing, so rejection leaves the old request unchanged. The starter overwrites accepted immediately and reports 1 0 0 0 for the sample instead of 3 0 2 2. Streaming directly into accepted is shorter but breaks rollback. The full HarborRoutes workshop adds stream failures, route search, witness checks, and output handling; external output cannot be rolled back merely by preserving in-memory state.
